commercial_incentive: Promotes CollegeVine's free account, GPA converter tool, and school list builder at the end
key_insights: States international applicants are often considered in a separate applicant pool from domestic students, so overall acceptance rates can differ sharply from international-specific rates
Cites UC Berkeley's overall acceptance rate as around 18% versus around 9% specifically for international applicants (illustrative example)

Notes recommendation letters, essays, and extracurriculars may be harder for admissions officers to evaluate for international students due to language/cultural differences, so test scores and grades may carry more relative weight

Advises international applicants provide an unweighted GPA (using a conversion tool if needed) since admissions officers recalculate transcripts on a common scale regardless of a school's native grading system
Recommends taking SAT/ACT even where optional, since submitting any score (even below average) may improve chances for international applicants specifically
Explains English proficiency testing (TOEFL or IELTS) is commonly required in addition to SAT/ACT if the student's high school instruction wasn't primarily in English

Notes financial aid is more limited for international students since they're ineligible for US federal aid; some schools are 'need-aware' for international admits (considering financial need in the admit decision), with only a few elite schools being fully need-blind for international students
Recommends building a 'spike' (a concentrated set of related achievements) in extracurriculars, especially valuable for standing out in the more competitive international applicant pool
specific_numbers_or_facts: UC Berkeley overall acceptance rate cited as ~18% vs. ~9% for international applicants (per video)
TOEFL described as taking roughly four and a half hours including registration, covering reading, listening, speaking, and writing
notable_or_distinctive: Directly quantifies the gap between a school's overall acceptance rate and its international-applicant-specific rate (Berkeley 18% vs 9%), a distinction often glossed over in general admissions content.
reliability_notes: Produced by a for-profit admissions platform (CollegeVine) with a promotional close; the Berkeley acceptance-rate figures are stated as illustrative examples without a cited source or year, so should be verified against current data.
